event.title: Death Outbreak
event.summary: An infant in Wisconsin has died from measles, marking the state's first measles-related death since 1990. This incident is also the third measles death reported in the United States within the same week, according to state health officials.

timeline.title: US Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years
timeline.summary: The United States has officially lost its measles elimination status for the first time in 26 years, as reported by international health officials. This loss is attributed to a resurgence of measles, primarily among unvaccinated populations, marking the highest transmission rates in over 30 years. The Pan American Health Organization confirmed that the US and Mexico have both lost their measles-free status.

event_overview.title: About Death Outbreak
event_overview.subject: Death Outbreak
event_overview.summary: This event is the renewed U.S. measles outbreak activity that began escalating in 2025 and continued through 2026, involving multiple state and local outbreaks rather than one single, geographically bounded incident. It includes both the health effects of sustained transmission and the public-health consequences of the United States no longer meeting the standard for measles elimination.

facts.label: Timeframe and geography
facts.value: The resurgence spans the United States, with large outbreaks reported since early 2025 and continued transmission during 2026; CDC’s national surveillance aggregates reports from state, local, tribal, and territorial jurisdictions.

facts.label: What counts as an outbreak
facts.value: For its national reporting, CDC defines a measles outbreak as three or more related cases; this means the wider event consists of numerous separate outbreaks and transmission chains.

facts.label: Public-health leadership
facts.value: State and local health departments lead case and outbreak investigations. CDC receives notified cases, monitors national data, provides laboratory and technical support, and can deploy assistance at the request of jurisdictions.

facts.label: Elimination standard
facts.value: Measles elimination means no continuous endemic transmission in a defined geographic area for at least 12 months with a well-performing surveillance system; re-established endemic transmission is a continuous chain lasting at least 12 months after prior elimination.

facts.label: Status change
facts.value: The United States had been declared free of endemic measles transmission in 2000. On November 17, 2026, CDC said it was working with partners to stop outbreaks and regain elimination status.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline tracks notable developments tied to the U.S. measles resurgence, including deaths and the elimination-status decision, rather than every case, local outbreak, exposure notice, or public-health response.
